errorCodes.meaning: The caller is not permitted to read memory in the named context.
The `keys` array contains the same key more than once. Refused rather than deduplicated, because a caller that sent a duplicate did not mean to.

purpose.description: The purpose the request named, when it named one.

purposeNamed.description: Whether the request named a purpose. False when it named none under an entry listing more than one.

errorCodes.meaning: The request names a purpose the caller's ACL entry does not grant, or names none under an entry listing more than one. The refusal discloses no memory content and is distinct from `contextForbidden`, which refuses access itself (VTI-ACL-104).

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MemoryKey.description: Agent-chosen identifier for an item within a context. Opaque to the maintainer: it MUST NOT be parsed, normalized, or case-folded, and prefix matching in `vta/memory/list` is a byte-prefix comparison over the UTF-8 encoding. Agents SHOULD use `/`-delimited hierarchical keys (`contact/billing`, `preference/timezone`) so that `prefix` can address a family of items, but the delimiter is a convention between an agent and itself. A key is content as well as an address: a key naming a person, a condition or a dispute discloses something to anyone who can list the context, even without its value.
MemoryKey.title: MemoryKey

MemoryPurpose.description: The one purpose for which the caller will use the memory content a request discloses (VTI-ACL-103): a name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (`personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining`) or an absolute IRI. The VTA grants it only if the caller's ACL entry does — `any` grants every purpose but `modelTraining` — refuses it otherwise (`purposeNotGranted`), and records it in the audit record of the read. Optional where the entry lists exactly one purpose (that one applies) or states `any` (the read is recorded as for no stated purpose).
MemoryPurpose.title: MemoryPurpose

MemoryRecord.description: A memory item as the maintainer holds it. `value` is absent in two distinct situations and a consumer MUST NOT conflate them: the item is a tombstone (`deleted` is true), or the caller asked for a metadata-only view (`vta/memory/list` without `includeValues`). This is why `deleted` is required rather than defaulted — a consumer that infers deletion from an absent value gets the tombstone case wrong exactly when convergence depends on it.

contextId.description: The VTA context the item is scoped to; the isolation boundary.

createdAt.description: When the item was first created at this key. MAY be absent on a tombstone whose body has been discarded, and on an item written before the maintainer kept versions.

deleted.description: True when this is a tombstone: the item was deleted, and this entry exists so that a consumer syncing incrementally learns of the deletion. Tombstones are reaped after the maintainer's retention window; see `vta/memory/list`.

deletedAt.description: When the item was deleted. Present only when `deleted` is true; equal to `updatedAt` for a tombstone the maintainer has not since rewritten.

updatedAt.description: When the write that produced this `version` was applied. For a tombstone, when the delete was applied.

value.description: The remembered text. Absent when this is a tombstone or a metadata-only view.

valueBytes.description: Size of the stored value in bytes over its UTF-8 encoding, as the maintainer measures it for the per-item cap. Present in metadata-only views so a consumer can decide what to fetch without fetching it; absent on a tombstone.

version.description: The context counter value this item's most recent write took. Supply it as `expectedVersion` on the next write to make that write conditional on nothing having changed in between.

MemoryRecord.title: MemoryRecord

MemoryValue.description: The remembered text: a fact, a summary, a preference. Opaque to the maintainer, which stores it as given and never interprets, rewrites or summarises it. The maintainer enforces a documented per-item cap on its size (see `vta/memory/put`).
MemoryValue.title: MemoryValue

MemoryVersion.description: A value of the context's monotonic write counter (see this schema's description). Server-assigned; a producer never chooses one.
MemoryVersion.title: MemoryVersion

Purpose.description: What content is used for: a lowerCamelCase name registered in the VTI specification's purpose registry (Appendix H) — `personalisation`, `taskExecution`, `analytics`, `modelTraining` at the time of writing — or an absolute IRI naming a purpose defined elsewhere, such as a purpose of the W3C Data Privacy Vocabulary (`https://w3id.org/dpv#ServicePersonalisation`). Compared by exact string equality: a consumer MUST NOT treat a purpose it does not recognise as equal to any other, and grants only a request naming exactly a listed purpose (VTI-ACL-109). A registered name is never an IRI, because it contains no `:`.
Purpose.title: Purpose

Response.description: Success response to vta/memory/get. Type https://trusttasks.org/spec/vta/memory/get/0.2#response. Every requested key appears in exactly one of `items`, `missing` or `deferred`, so a caller can account for all of them without comparing sets itself.

deferred.description: Requested keys the maintainer did not evaluate because the response had reached its size budget. The caller re-requests exactly these. A deferred key was not read, and a maintainer MUST NOT record it as read.

items.description: The items found, each with its `value` (a tombstone has none), in the order the keys were requested. May be empty.

missing.description: Requested keys holding no item — and, unless `includeDeleted` was set, keys holding only a tombstone. Reported rather than silently omitted.

schema.description: Recall up to 256 named memory items from one context in a single round trip. The read an agent makes when it knows what it needs, and the one whose audit record says exactly which items it saw.

contextId.description: The VTA context the items are scoped to; the isolation boundary.

includeDeleted.description: Defaults to false. When true, a key holding a tombstone yields an item with `deleted: true` rather than appearing in `missing`.

keys.description: The keys to recall. Duplicates are refused rather than deduplicated, because a caller that sent one did not mean to and would otherwise never find out.

purpose.description: OPTIONAL. The one purpose the caller will use the content this request discloses for (VTI-ACL-103). Granted only as the caller's ACL entry grants it; a purpose the entry does not grant is refused with `purposeNotGranted`. May be omitted where the entry lists exactly one purpose, or states `any`.

schema.title: VTA Memory Get — payload
